01_nri_hazard_ranking: FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025), Charleston County. Composite risk score 98.6 (Relatively High); total EAL $500 M per year; social vulnerability Relatively Low; community resilience Very High.
02_nri_sc_county_ranking: National Risk Index composite risk for all 46 South Carolina counties.
03_disaster_declarations: All FEMA disaster declarations that designated Charleston County (27), OpenFEMA.
04_storm_events_summary: NOAA NCEI Storm Events, Charleston County and its forecast zones, 1996 to 2026 (31 years). Damage in nominal dollars as reported; not inflation-adjusted.
05_nfip_claims_by_year: NFIP redacted claims, Charleston County: 19,289 claims, $312.2 M paid (nominal), 1978 to 2026.
06_nfip_claims_by_zone: Claims by rated flood zone: a large share outside the A and V zones shows flooding beyond the 1% annual chance floodplain.
07_nfip_top_flood_events: The 15 named flood events with the largest NFIP payments in Charleston County.
08_repetitive_loss_by_community: NFIP multiple-loss properties (1,296): repetitive loss (RL) and severe repetitive loss (SRL), with how many are mitigated.
09_earthquakes_m3_200km: USGS ComCat earthquakes of magnitude 3 or more within 200 km of Charleston, including the 1886 event.
10_hma_subapplications: FEMA Hazard Mitigation Assistance subapplications benefiting Charleston County (106), by program and hazard.
11_hm_plan_status: Status of the current Charleston County multi-jurisdictional hazard mitigation plan (OpenFEMA).
27_nfip_community_status: NFIP participation, first FIRM date, effective map date and Community Rating System class of each community (OpenFEMA Community Status Book).
12_building_inventory: USACE National Structure Inventory, Charleston County: every structure, replacement values in 2022-era dollars as published by the NSI.
13_flood_exposure_by_jurisdiction: Structures, value (structure plus contents) and night-time population in each FEMA flood zone, by jurisdiction. SFHA = VE plus A zones.
14_flood_exposure_by_occupancy: Flood exposure by occupancy group and flood zone.
15_critical_facilities_flood: Critical facility structures by type and flood zone, identified from NSI occupancy classes (COM6, RES6, EDU1, EDU2, GOV1, GOV2); a facility campus can count as several structures.
16_social_vulnerability_flood: Flood exposure in census tracts in the top quartile of the CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index (2022, ranked within South Carolina).
26_first_floor_check_nfip: Check of first-floor elevations against NFIP claims that carry an elevation-certificate rating (lowest floor minus BFE). NFIP-rated buildings are a biased sample (insured, mostly post-FIRM), but the NSI's default foundation heights put far too many buildings below the BFE, so the adjusted (pre/post-FIRM) elevations are the central estimate and the NSI defaults an upper bound.
17_hazus_flood_scenarios: Hazus flood depth-damage loss for the 1% annual chance flood from the effective FIRM base flood elevations, and the same flood with 1 to 3 ft of sea-level rise added (applied only inside today's SFHA, so the rise scenarios undercount). Depth in a structure = BFE minus first-floor elevation; post-FIRM structures are taken at today's BFE plus the NFIP-measured median freeboard (see table 26). The last row uses the NSI's default foundation heights for every structure and is an upper bound. Water below the first floor still causes the small losses the Hazus curves give for negative depths.
18_hazus_flood_by_jurisdiction: Hazus 1% annual chance flood loss by jurisdiction (structure and contents).
19_hazus_flood_by_occupancy: Hazus 1% annual chance flood loss by occupancy group.
20_hazus_flood_ddfs_used: The Hazus depth-damage functions applied, with how many damaged structures used each.
21_hazus_eq_summary: Hazus earthquake building damage from equivalent-PGA fragility curves (Hazus EQ v6.1) and building repair-cost ratios for the 1886 ShakeMap; expected numbers of structures in each damage state. Structural, building-only loss; no contents, casualties, debris or liquefaction.
21b_hazus_eq_sensitivity: How much the earthquake loss depends on the assumed seismic design levels and on the ShakeMap ground motion (which for 1886 is inferred from felt-intensity reports, not instruments).
22_hazus_eq_by_jurisdiction: Hazus earthquake damage and loss for the 1886 scenario by jurisdiction.
23_hazus_eq_by_building_type: Hazus earthquake damage by model building type and seismic design level (assigned from the NSI's general construction type, stories and year built).
24_eq_shaking_exposure: Exposure to 1886-scenario shaking intensity (Modified Mercalli Intensity from the ShakeMap).
25_tract_risk_profile: Census-tract risk profile: NRI composite risk and hazard EAL, CDC SVI, and this study's Hazus flood and earthquake losses.
